papers.title: Comment on egusphere-2026-2859
papers.abstract: Abstract. Ongoing climate warming is impacting the frequency and magnitude of extreme weather. The high sensitivity of snow to changes in temperature and precipitation makes it a primary indicator of climate change. Previous studies have proven that the snow cover extent has decreased with rapid warming. Nevertheless, this remains controversial, and no solid conclusion has been reached regarding snow depth changes. Numerous remote sensing‐based approaches have been used to derive spatially continuous snow depth. However, challenges remain in capturing and understanding the spatial variability of snow depth because of the non-linear and so-called ‘ill-posed’ problems associated with inversion framework. Machine learning (ML) techniques (including deep learning) are beginning to play important roles in advancing snow depth retrieval with microwave remote sensing, owing to their strong ability to fit nonlinear, nonexplicit functional relationships between snow depth and massive amounts of geoscience data. However, a systematic review of ML applications in snow depth retrieval with remote sensing is notably absent from the literature, and the trajectory for future advancements remains ambiguous. This review comprehensively summarizes the implementation and progress of snow depth research using microwave remote sensing over the last decade (2015–2025), and analyzes current research directions and areas where further developments are needed. An analysis of the literature reveals that the number of ML-related articles has increased over the past 10 years, rising from 3 to 33. By first-author affiliation, China and the United States lead in terms of contributions, accounting for almost 70 % of papers. We also found that western countries are actively engaged in high-resolution snow depth retrieval (ranging from meter to hundreds of metres) at regional or catchment scales (especially over mountains), which is attributed to their dense and comprehensive ground-based and airborne field campaigns (e.g., SnowEx, NoSREx, and ASO Lidar etc.). While China focuses on snow depth retrieval at the global scale or regional scales, typically at a coarse spatial resolution (10 or 25…

papers.title: MODELAGEM HIPSOMÉTRICA COM USO DE COVARIÁVEIS EM FLORESTA ESTACIONAL SEMIDECIDUAL
papers.abstract: Objetivou-se avaliar o desempenho de modelos tradicionais e mistos no ajuste da relação hipsométrica em fragmento de Floresta Estacional Semidecidual, utilizando dados de 19 unidades amostrais localizadas no Parque Estadual de Nova Baden, em Lambari, Minas Gerais. Foram criados cenários: um a partir do banco de dados original e outro após a exclusão de pontos discrepantes, para ajustes de modelos de relação hipsométrica, que foram avaliados por meio do coeficiente de determinação ajustado, do erro padrão da estimativa, dos critérios de informação de Akaike e Bayesiano, da análise gráfica de resíduos, do teste F e da significância dos coeficientes. A melhor equação foi submetida à inclusão das covariáveis espécie, família botânica e classe de diâmetro, consideradas como efeitos aleatórios. O modelo linear de Trorey foi considerado o mais preciso em ambos os cenários. A remoção dos pontos discrepantes resultou em estimativas mais precisas e menos tendenciosas, que, quando associadas à modelagem mista, com a inclusão do fator aleatório “espécie” nos três coeficientes do modelo, propiciaram um aumento de 18% no coeficiente de determinação ajustado e uma redução de 7,2% no erro padrão da estimativa. Palavras-chave: relação altura-diâmetro; modelos mistos; floresta nativa. Hypsometric modeling using covariates in a semideciduous seasonal forest ABSTRACT: The objective of this study was to evaluate the performance of traditional and mixed models in fitting the hypsometric relationship in a fragment of Semideciduous Seasonal Forest, using data from 19 sample plots located in Nova Baden State Park, in Lambari, Minas Gerais, Brazil. Two scenarios were developed: one based on the original database and another after removing outliers, for fitting hypsometric relationship models. The models were evaluated using the adjusted coefficient of determination, standard error of the estimate, Akaike Information Criterion, Bayesian Information Criterion, graphical residual analysis, F-test, and coefficient significance. The best equation was then extended to include covariates such as species, botanical family, and diameter class, considered as random effects. The Trorey linear mode…

papers.title: Developing an analysis-ready data processing framework for SWOT-derived inland surface water products
papers.abstract: The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission provides new opportunities for inland water monitoring by observing surface water extent and water surface elevation (WSE). However, the direct use of SWOT Level-2 HR Raster products for surface water mapping remains limited by fragmented water patterns, random noise, mixed pixels, and systematic stripe artifacts. To improve product usability, this study develops an analysis-ready data (ARD) processing framework for SWOT-derived inland surface water products, with emphasis on surface water extent and water-mask structure rather than independent WSE accuracy validation. The framework integrates wse_qual, wse_uncert, water_frac, water_area, sig0, dark_frac, and layover_impact for multi-parameter filtering and spatial structure optimization, where WSE-related variables are used as product-native quality indicators. Dongting Lake was selected as the study area, and Sentinel-1 SAR-derived water masks were used only as reference data for water-extent consistency and spatial-structure assessment. Results show that ARD processing moderately improves the water-extent agreement between SWOT-derived water masks and the Sentinel-1 reference. IoU increases from 0.2926 to 0.4081, Precision from 0.3203 to 0.5154, and F1-score from 0.4527 to 0.5796, while Recall decreases from 0.7718 to 0.6621, indicating a trade-off between reducing false positives and preserving reference water pixels. Spatial fragmentation is also substantially reduced: connected components decrease from 18,187 to 557, the small-patch area ratio drops from 5.63% to 0, and boundary density declines from 0.0048 to 0.0034. The persistence of along-track stripe artifacts represents a central constraint of the current ARD framework, indicating that geometry-related systematic errors require additional correction beyond pixel-level filtering and spatial optimization. Overall, the proposed framework improves the analysis readiness of SWOT-derived inland surface water products for water mapping and flood monitoring.

papers.title: HIGH-PRECISION CRACK WIDTH MEASUREMENT IN REINFORCED CONCRETE USING MOBILE LIDAR AND POINT CLOUD ANALYSIS
papers.abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of consumer-grade mobile LiDAR systems for measuring crack widths on a laboratory-tested reinforced concrete (RC) beam specimen. The observed cracks correspond to flexural surface cracks formed under vertical loading. A comprehensive workflow was developed, incorporating geometric calibration using spatial measurement targets (SMTs), photogrammetric validation, and comparative analysis across six mobile LiDAR applications. Calibration tests demonstrated that SMT-supported scans achieved sub-millimeter accuracy, with average deviations around ±0.50 mm, while unreferenced scans showed errors exceeding 1.5 mm. Crack width measurements performed in CloudCompare and AutoCAD showed strong agreement with reference visual measurements, confirming the suitability of LiDAR-derived point clouds for quantitative crack assessment. Comparative evaluation of mobile applications revealed that Canvas, RealityScan, and Scaniverse produced the most accurate and homogeneous point distributions, enabling reliable sub-millimeter measurements. In contrast, high-density outputs from PIX4Dcatch and Sitescape resulted in overestimated crack widths due to point clustering and surface layering effects. The results highlight the importance of geometric calibration, point cloud distribution quality, and scanning protocols in achieving accurate and repeatable crack width measurements. Overall, the proposed methodology demonstrates the potential of mobile LiDAR technology as a low-cost and practical tool for quantitative surface crack assessment in structural health monitoring applications.

papers.title: World-Making
papers.abstract: World(s) in process.World-making (or worldmaking) separates and binds together worlds and ways of making.World-making in the context of machine vision complicates visual repre sen ta tions of worlds in relation to the modalities of their creation and perception.Often fictive, obscure, or manipulative, these images cannot be considered apart from their specific technological contexts, as they are "part of a broader system of analy sis, identification, tracking, and destruction" (Parikka 2023, vi).The particularity of thinking machine vision and world-making together resides not only in what and how a world appears and becomes visually perceivable but also and especially in all that remains invisible (to the human eye).Media theorist Jussi Parikka (2023) offers an in-depth account of the role of invisuality-the agency of optical regimes and their spaces-in his recent book Operational Images: From the Visual to the Invisual.Importantly for this discussion, he explains that the notion of the invisual is less about a move from human to machine and more about a dif fer ent mode of perception.Here, he refers to the collaborative work of sociologist Adrian MacKenzie and art and design professor Anna Munster, who highlight ongoing perceptual transformations: "While visual techniques and practices continue to proliferate-from data visualization to LiDAR technologies for capturing non-optical images-the visual itself as a paradigm for how to see and observe is being evacuated, and that space is now occupied by a differ ent kind of perception" (MacKenzie and Muster 2019, 6).They are interested in the operative potential of images, and their argument-like Parikka's-is a move beyond machine vision toward operations performed through platforms, models, and datasets.The possibilities for observation and the sensing of change through technical advancements also play into techniques of world-making, the coexistential dimension of planetary scale (Reed 2019) and the sensory capacities of capturing and recording devices.The creation of world versions is not dependent solely on choices regarding editing, camera movement, zooming, papers.title: Vertical distribution of prey and vegetation structure shape bat and ground-dwelling mammal activity in a temperate forest
papers.abstract: Vertical structural complexity shapes resource availability throughout forest ecosystems. However, how mobile consumers respond to this variation across the vertical profile remains poorly understood, particularly for taxonomic groups differing in their ability to access different vertical layers. In this study, we examine how the activity of flying and ground-dwelling small mammals respond to resource distribution and stand structure across the vertical forest profile. We combined paired acoustic bat surveys conducted in the canopy and understorey with ground-based camera trap surveys of small, ground-dwelling mammals, alongside layer-specific measurements of invertebrate prey abundance and LiDAR-derived vegetation structure. Bat activity varied across the vertical profile in line with known foraging ecomorphology; open and edge-foraging specialists were more frequently detected in the canopy, while forest-interior foraging species were more frequently detected in the understorey. Across mammal taxonomic groups, dietary specialists tracked invertebrate abundance independently of vertical layer, whereas dietary generalists showed no relationship to prey abundance. This suggests that trophic specialisation, rather than locomotion mode, determines the strength of bottom-up coupling between invertebrates and their mammalian predators. In contrast, the structural drivers of activity differed strongly between the two taxonomic groups and vertical layers, indicating that structural niche partitioning does not follow the same rules as trophic coupling. Bat activity showed a clutter-versus-resource trade-off and ground-level structural conditions shaped ground-dwelling mammal activity more strongly than canopy-associated attributes. These results show that structural niche partitioning in forest consumer communities is determined by taxon-specific structural characteristics rather than by a single common gradient of habitat quality. Vertically explicit sampling designs are therefore essential to avoid incomplete inference about the environmental drivers of activity, especially for canopy-associated species.

papers.title: TreeCLIP: a source-controlled evaluation of frozen 2D foundation-model features for tree-species clustering from LiDAR
papers.abstract: Complete code, configuration, result files, and the pre-registration of the frozen 3D baseline for the manuscript Frozen 2D Foundation-Model Features Cluster Tree Species in LiDAR Point Clouds More Coherently Than the Evaluated Geometric Descriptors: A Source-Controlled Evaluation (under revision at PFG – Journal of Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Geoinformation Science; preprint DOI: 10.21203/rs.3.rs-10238136/v1). The pipeline renders each individual-tree LiDAR point cloud into six PCA-aligned height-coded depth views, encodes them with frozen 2D vision foundation models (CLIP, DINOv2, supervised-ImageNet, and random-init controls), and evaluates unsupervised species clustering under matched dimensions with acquisition-source confounding treated as a first-class control (within-source residuals, per-block and leave-one-source-out analyses, and a pre-registered frozen 3D OpenShape/PointBERT baseline). Every number in the manuscript traces to a JSON result file under runs/protocol_v2/gen/ in this archive. The point-cloud datasets themselves are not redistributed; the README lists their DOIs and licenses. MIT license.
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

papers.title: Do green roofs support urban bird diversity? Evidence from citizen science observations in Shanghai
papers.abstract: Green roofs hold substantial potential for supporting urban biodiversity conservation. Researchers have investigated how multidimensional characteristics of green roofs (e.g., 2D spatial and 3D structural features) influence habitat suitability for urban avifauna. Nevertheless, reliance on labor-intensive field surveys for bird observations has confined research to finite scales. Additionally, oversimplified proxies for vegetation structure (e.g., coverage and average height) overlook the structural complexity jointly formed by vegetation with divergent morphologies. To address these limitations, this study integrates citizen-science bird data with remote-sensing-derived roof metrics in Shanghai, applying Negative Binomial (NB) and Zero-inflated NB models to investigate the associations between multidimensional roof features and bird abundance and species richness at large scales across multiple buffers, while accounting for adjacent greenspace features and observation effort. Results show modest improvements in model performance when roof- and greenspace-level variables were considered jointly, suggesting that roof attributes may provide limited but complementary explanatory information beyond surrounding greenspace conditions. Roof-level associations and cross-level interactions with both avian metrics were more evident within 125 and 250 m buffers, but their direction and magnitude varied across spatial scales and surrounding landscape context, indicating scale dependence and context sensitivity. Several roof factors, including NDVI, relative land surface temperature, woody vegetation cover, and 3D vegetation structure, exhibited nonlinear or conditional associations with avian metrics. In particular, associations involving roof 3D vegetation structure varied with roof floor, roof grass coverage, and surrounding vegetation cover. Our findings advance large-scale understanding of roof-bird associations and underscore the importance of jointly considering both horizontal and vertical structural elements within a multiscale framework. The study provides evidence-based insights for designing biodiversity-friendly green roofs that consider broader urban vegetatio…

papers.title: Model–Observation Discrepancies in the Coupling of Vegetation Greening and Transpiration Under Rising Vapor Pressure Deficit
papers.abstract: Abstract Vapor pressure deficit (VPD), a key indicator of atmospheric dryness, has markedly increased across most global land areas due to progressive warming. Although site‐scale studies show that increasing VPD may enhance plant transpiration (Tran) and influence water and energy fluxes between land and atmosphere, this relationship has not been thoroughly investigated on the global scale. Here, we apply a binning approach to quantify the contribution of VPD to global Tran by ruling out the effect of soil moisture. To this aim, we integrate satellite‐based observations, reanalysis data sets, and simulations from sixteen Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) models into a coherent framework. VPD shows a broadly positive influence on Tran over most parts of the global land consistently across all data sets. Exceptions occur in tropical rainforests where reanalysis data and CMIP6 model outputs suggest a negative VPD‐Tran interplay. Attribution analysis suggests that increasing leaf area index reduces the positive effect of VPD on Tran in reanalysis data sets and CMIP6 models compared to satellite‐based observations. This discrepancy may reflect differences in the representation of the effective canopy‐level response to high atmospheric water demand, potentially involving stomatal regulation, plant hydraulics, and vegetation structure. Such differences may contribute to an underestimated transpiration response to VPD. These findings highlight the need to better represent physiological processes, hydraulic processes, and vegetation structural characteristics in process‐based models to capture vegetation responses to increasing water stress.
keywords: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

papers.title: Simultaneous ToF/FMCW LiDAR Using a Dual‐Mode Light Source in a Single Architecture
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Light detection and ranging (LiDAR) systems are increasingly required to provide long‐range operation, high axial resolution, and velocity estimation within a single platform. However, conventional time‐of‐flight (ToF) and frequency‐modulated continuous‐wave (FMCW) methods demand a high electrical bandwidth to satisfy these requirements simultaneously. Here, we present a simultaneous ToF/FMCW LiDAR enabled by a dual‐mode light source that alternately generates nanosecond pulses and FMCW waveforms through synchronized optical‐intensity and frequency‐modulation. This single‐architecture design enables concurrent acquisition of time‐domain ToF and spectral‐domain FMCW ranging without additional optical paths or auxiliary light sources. Under bandwidth‐limited conditions, ToF measurement maintained absolute distance accuracy despite a loss of resolution, whereas the FMCW measurement preserved high axial resolution but experienced aliasing due to subsampling. By integrating these complementary datasets through a reconstruction algorithm, the system achieves high‐resolution short‐range performance together with alias‐free long‐range detection. Moreover, Doppler analysis of the FMCW interferograms verified accurate velocity estimation within the Nyquist limit. These results demonstrate that a dual‐mode light source can unify ToF and FMCW ranging in a compact single architecture, overcoming electrical bandwidth constraints while enabling simultaneous distance and velocity measurements.

papers.title: Toward Consistent Canopy Characterization From Low‐Cost UAV Imagery
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Monitoring tropical forest structure at landscape scale requires cost‐effective methods capable of bridging the gap between field inventories and satellite remote sensing products. However, the diversity of available individual tree crown (ITC) segmentation algorithms raises questions about the consistency and reliability of derived structural metrics—a critical issue for any ecological application relying on these outputs. We evaluated three ITC segmentation algorithms—Detectree2, SAM, and the hybrid Detectree2SAM (D2S)—applied to very high‐resolution RGB orthomosaics (5 cm resolution) acquired over ~200 ha of the Luki Biosphere Reserve (Democratic Republic of Congo) using a low‐cost drone. Algorithms were validated at the individual scale against a photointerpretation reference of 1882 manually delineated crowns and at the plot scale against a field inventory of 360 trees across 18 plots. At the individual scale, IoU‐based F1 scores ranged from 0.57 (D2S) to 0.67 (SAM), revealing clear precision–recall trade‐offs. At the plot scale, D2S provided the most accurate crown area estimates (RMSD = 26%–29%), while SAM best reproduced canopy density (RMSD = 22%). All three algorithms systematically overestimated aggregated metrics; a linear correction substantially reduced prediction errors and improved cross‐algorithm convergence, yielding consistent estimates—median crown area of the 20 largest trees (~148 m 2 ), total crown area (~3850 m 2 per plot), and canopy density (~80 ind/ha). Agreement maps revealed systematic spatial divergences, including edge artifacts, SAM's tendency to underestimate canopy density, and localized overestimation of crown areas in disturbed stands. Raw ITC outputs carry substantial systematic biases requiring explicit field‐calibrated correction before ecological use. We propose a three‐step operational pipeline—(i) plot‐scale field validation, (ii) per‐algorithm linear bias correction, and (iii) landscape‐scale aggregation—that reduces inter‐algorithm divergence and delivers consistent, ecologically interpretable structural estimates from low‐cost UAV imagery.

papers.title: Cross-species evaluation: Reindeer as an ecological evaluator of a satellite-based lichen cover map
papers.abstract: Accurate maps of resources are important tools in wildlife and animal range management yet validating them across large spatial extents remains a challenge. We leveraged fine-scale GPS tracking of consumers and a strong consumer-resource relationship to perform large-scale evaluation of a resource map. Our aim was to present the first high-resolution ground lichen cover map for the Sámi reindeer winter grazing area in Sweden, and to complement traditional model validation methods by using 680,000 reindeer GPS relocations and the consumer-resource relationship between reindeer ( Rangifer tarandus tarandus ) and ground lichens for ecological evaluation. We expected a successful map to be reflected in the reindeer use of lichen, and that predicted lichen cover would be a significant predictor in habitat selection models. The map was produced using a Generalised Additive Model trained on National Forest Inventory field data with Sentinel-2 imagery, forest variables, and soil type as predictors. The model explained 57.4% of the total variance in lichen cover. Our analyses supported both expectations: hurdle models showed that the odds of predicted lichen presence were 44% higher at reindeer-used than available locations, and used locations had 15% more predicted lichen cover than available locations. Integrated step-selection analyses confirmed consistent selection for predicted lichen cover, and adding the lichen map outperformed a simpler model including topographic and movement variables. Best performance was achieved combining predicted lichen cover with land cover classification. Our cross-species evaluation approach offers a complement to traditional statistical validation, applicable to other systems with strong consumer-resource relationships.

papers.title: Composite Degradation Index Reveals Type-Specific Drivers of Forest Decline on Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
papers.abstract: Forest degradation assessments are constrained by single-dimensional indicators (e.g., NDVI) that fail to simultaneously capture functional degradation (biomass loss) and structural degradation (landscape fragmentation), while type-specific management responses remain poorly operationalized. To address this gap, we developed a Composite Degradation Index (CDI) integrating biomass dynamics (Biomass Slope) and a forest fragmentation index (FFI). The CDI was applied at a 30 m spatial resolution using MODIS NDVI/EVI, SRTM DEM, and land-use data from 2000 to 2020 across coniferous, broad-leaved, and mixed forests across the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP) to quantify degradation severity, identify nonlinear response thresholds, and project fragmentation trends under CMIP6 scenarios using natural breaks classification. Random Forest, XGBoost, and SHAP analysis disentangled the relative contributions of climatic factors, topography, and human activities. The CDI improved assessment accuracy by 22% relative to NDVI. Coniferous forests exhibited strong sensitivity to warming (5.2% per +1 °C), with 27% of degradation indirectly linked to permafrost thaw. Broad-leaved forests responded most strongly to precipitation variability (3.8% per +10%), reflecting hydraulic stress and habitat connectivity loss. Mixed forests showed the highest anthropogenic degradation (35% contribution), highlighting ecotonal fragmentation. Under SSP5-8.5, severe fragmentation is projected to reach 21.73% by 2060; moderate mitigation delays extreme fragmentation by 1.6 years. The CDI provides a transferable framework for “threshold diagnosis–attribution–zoning intervention” in the QTP and analogous vulnerable ecosystems. Based on type-specific response thresholds, we propose three management strategies: (i) permafrost monitoring and thermal buffering for coniferous forests; (ii) hydrological connectivity conservation for broad-leaved forests; and (iii) anthropogenic disturbance buffers for mixed forests. This study demonstrates that composite indicators can bridge environmental monitoring and sustainability decision-making, directly contributing to SDG 13 and SDG 15.

papers.title: Dynamicity of Stand‐Scale Transpiration and Its Controlling Factors: Insights From Mixed‐Conifer Mediterranean Headwater Catchments
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The mixed‐conifer forests of Sierra Nevada create a complex system of water, energy and nutrient cycling. Thus, this study aims to understand the spatial and temporal variability of soil moisture and stand‐scale transpiration across three central Sierra headwater catchments and their controlling factors. The mean daily average sap flow of Abies concolor varies from 0.69 ± 0.48 to 1.27 ± 0.72 L/h. Higher spatial variability in soil moisture and stand‐scale transpiration was found in the snowmelt period, followed by the soil moisture recession period when vegetation growth is not water limited. The daily average sap flow was higher on south aspect than on north aspect, but this pattern was not consistent across all seasons. The diel pattern of the sap flow revealed a larger contribution of nocturnal sap flow during the dry period (22.3%–37.8%) and a smaller contribution during the recession period (16.3%–23.9%) across all catchments. Multiple linear regression analysis suggests that sap flow during summer (recession period) was governed by the ecosystem's energy, indicated in part by vapour pressure deficit and temperature. Soil moisture regulated the subsequent dry‐period transpiration. The energy‐limited condition in winter restricted the transpiration even when sufficient soil moisture was available. Topography, explained by topographic positioning index ( tpi ), played a major role in explaining stand‐scale transpiration, especially during higher atmospheric demand periods, whereas tree size (i.e., DBH) explained more than 10% sap flow variance in all seasons. The findings of this study will provide the basis for a better understanding of the eco‐hydrological processes of the Sierra Nevada under natural and anthropogenic‐induced changes.
keywords: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

papers.title: Assessing the resilience of coastal vegetation ecosystem through carbon storage dynamics using Landsat time series
papers.abstract: Due to increasing habitat fragmentation and persistent land-cover dynamics, assessing resilience in coastal vegetation ecosystems poses substantial challenges. To address these issues, this study quantifies the spatiotemporal dynamics and driving mechanisms of vegetation carbon storage to evaluate ecosystem resilience in complex coastal habitats. By integrating long-term Landsat time-series data on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform with the Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs (InVEST) model, we developed an integrated framework for assessing coastal vegetation resilience. Taking the coastal zone of Jiangsu Province as the study area, the results indicate the following: (1) By integrating critical factors such as phenological variability, tidal inundation, and land–water interactions, the proposed model significantly improves the accuracy of vegetation information extraction and the reliability of long-term carbon storage monitoring in complex coastal environments; (2) From 1985 to 2024, the total vegetation carbon storage in Jiangsu Province exhibited a fluctuating upward trend, rising from 1258.08 Tg to 1514.41 Tg, marking a net gain of 256.33 Tg (20.38 %). This suggests that coastal vegetation maintains robust long-term carbon sequestration capacity amid cultivated land dominance and enhanced forest carbon sinks; (3) Spatially, the evolution of vegetation carbon storage revealed a distinct pattern of “North–South differentiation and Land–Sea coupling.” Specifically, the northern plains and coastal zones showed continuous growth and steadily strengthened carbon sink functions, whereas the highly urbanized southern region experienced greater constraints and more pronounced fluctuations. Resilience assessments indicated stronger recovery elasticity and maintenance capacity in the north, relatively weaker resilience and higher sensitivity to disturbances in the south, and a transitional coastal type characterized by high recovery potential but weak stability; (4) The provincial-scale increase in vegetation carbon storage was primarily driven by the structural upgrading of vegetation coverage classes. Specifically, the significant expansi…

papers.title: Autonomous UAVs in Critical Infrastructure Inspection: Empirical Evaluation, Reporting Standard, and Implications for Strategic Decisions
papers.abstract: Purpose: Autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become a mature tool for remote sensing data acquisition for critical infrastructure (IC) inspections, particularly in the energy, transportation, bridge infrastructure, water networks and industrial installation sectors.The aim of the article is to synthetically capture the results of empirical research: field inspection missions using RGB, thermal imaging (TIR) and LiDAR sensors, as well as automatic data analytics (deep learning) to detect defects and anomalies.Design/Methodology/Approach: In the methodological part, a unified scheme for reporting empirical research (mission parameters, method of obtaining the "reference truth", quality metrics and operational utility indicators) is proposed, as well as a framework for integrating results with crisis management processes (time-to-assessment, false dispositions, repair priorities).

papers.title: Annual canopy height mapping in Italy from Landsat and multi-source LiDAR for disturbance and recovery monitoring
papers.abstract: Accurate and continuous monitoring of forest canopy height is essential for assessing forest structure, biomass, disturbance, and recovery. However, airborne laser scanning (ALS) has incomplete national coverage, is updated infrequently, and is costly to acquire. Here, we present an annual 30 m canopy height dataset for Italy spanning 2004–2024, developed by integrating Landsat imagery with multi-source LiDAR observations in a time-series deep learning framework. Two U-Net models were trained independently using canopy height reference data from ALS and NASA's Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) spaceborne LiDAR mission. Annual canopy height predictions from the two models were then fused using Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) to improve spatial consistency and temporal continuity. Validation against field measurements from the Italian National Forest Inventory (NFI) showed high predictive accuracy, with a mean absolute error of 3.98 m. Despite its coarser spatial resolution, our 30 m product outperformed canopy height products currently available in Italy, including a Europe-scale PlanetScope-based dataset at 3 m resolution and a global Sentinel-based canopy height product at 10 m resolution, while also providing a harmonized annual record over two decades rather than only one or a few years. In contrast, an existing Europe-scale Landsat-based product yielded a low R 2 in this mountainous region, highlighting the limited transferability of broad-scale models in complex terrain. To demonstrate the utility of the dataset for forest dynamics monitoring, we derived a canopy height change-based disturbance product and evaluated it against independent observed events, obtaining a mean precision of 0.64 for 2005–2016. We also quantified post-disturbance recovery by tracking canopy height regrowth in areas disturbed during 2004–2005 across major Italian biomes through 2024. These results show that combining Landsat time series, multi-source LiDAR, deep learning, and Bayesian fusion provides an effective framework for annual canopy height mapping and for monitoring forest disturbance and recovery. The final dataset is publicly available via Zenodo and offers a…

papers.title: Intercomparison of Global Solar Induced Chlorophyl Fluorescence Products
papers.abstract: Abstract Satellite observations of Sun‐Induced Chlorophyll Fluorescence (SIF) provide a powerful means to assess terrestrial photosynthesis at regional to global scales, yet major SIF products differ in retrieval strategy, radiometric stability, and sensitivity to environmental conditions. We evaluate four widely used SIF data sets—Continuous Solar‐Induced Fluorescence (CSIF), Global OCO‐2 SIF (GOSIF), SIF005, and OCO‐005—across multiple biomes, climate regimes, and temporal scales by comparing them against tower‐derived gross primary production (GPP), tower‐observed SIF, and independent climate anomalies. Across FLUXNET sites, all SIF data sets show robust linear relationships with annual GPP ( R 2 = 0.64–0.71), with strongest performance in forested ecosystems and increased scatter in water‐limited landscapes. Monthly analyses in northern high latitudes reveal exceptionally strong SIF–GPP coupling ( R 2 up to 0.87), demonstrating SIF's ability to capture rapid seasonal transitions in boreal and tundra productivity. Drought evaluations in the Sahel and Amazon show that GOSIF and Continuous Solar‐Induced Fluorescence (CSIF) most accurately track rainfall‐driven reductions in photosynthesis, while SIF005 displays weaker and noisier responses. Long‐term trend analyses north of 50°N reveal consistent early‐ and late‐season productivity increases in GOSIF, CSIF, and FLUXCOM‐X GPP, whereas SIF005 diverges substantially, underscoring limitations for climate‐trend detection in high‐latitude environments. Comparisons with tower‐measured SIF further confirm the physical fidelity of the satellite data sets, with GOSIF and OCO‐005 showing the strongest agreement. Overall, SIF is a reliable proxy for ecosystem productivity across diverse environmental settings, but performance varies among products. CSIF and GOSIF generally showed the most consistent behavior across seasons, climatic extremes, and regions, whereas SIF005 exhibited greater noise and less consistent trend behavior.
keywords: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

papers.title: Tree-neighborhood scale structure–radiation coupling analysis and modeling using multi-source remote sensing and ensemble learning
papers.abstract: Forest structure regulates the spatial heterogeneity of absorbed photosynthetically active radiation (APAR), thereby shaping ecosystem functioning and productivity. However, how neighborhood spatial configuration and competition dynamics control APAR distribution remains poorly understood, particularly in structurally heterogeneous and topographically complex natural forests. To address this, we proposed FASAR (Forest Architecture–Solar Absorption Response), a structure–radiation coupling framework for complex-terrain natural forests. FASAR establishes an integrated workflow for structure–radiation coupling analysis by integrating multi-source LiDAR-based structural parameterization, Adaptive Leaf Synthesis Algorithm (ALSA)-assisted 3D forest reconstruction, 3D radiative transfer simulation, and structure-stratified ensemble modeling. It converts heterogeneous forest architecture into plot-, neighborhood-, and tree-level descriptors and links these descriptors with spatially explicit APAR patterns. Applied to 144 plots (5.76 ha, 3,417 trees) in a natural Qinghai spruce forest in western China, FASAR revealed that large trees absorb more light with vertically stable patterns, while canopy stratification, competition, and size disparity intensify vertical displacement of light and suppress central-tree absorption. Structural dominance and near-natural spatial configurations enhanced APAR interception (ρ = 0.08–0.49, p < 0.001), while moderate aggregation and openness improved light scattering (ρ = 0.06–0.19, p < 0.001). Slope (ρ = –0.37, p < 0.001) and gap density (ρ = –0.18, p < 0.05) showed dual facilitation–inhibition effects on mean APAR. Structure-specific Bagging models achieved moderate performance (R 2 = 0.457–0.546). Variable importance analysis identified crown area (CA) as the dominant driver across all structural types (contribution: 68.95–81.78 %), followed by tree height, spatial density, and other structural heterogeneity indices. This framework provides an operational pathway for quantifying how neighborhood-scale forest architecture regulates individual-tree light absorption under complex-terrain conditions. The structure–radiation mechanisms rev…
papers.venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
keywords: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

papers.title: Quantifying Post-Earthquake Urban Green Space Loss Using an Optimized Deep Learning-Based Semantic Segmentation Framework
papers.abstract: Large-scale earthquakes and the rapid reconstruction processes that follow lead to significant spatial transformations in urban ecosystems, particularly exerting pronounced impacts on intra-urban green spaces. This study quantitatively evaluates changes in urban green areas that occurred after the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes in Hatay (Antakya) and Elazığ (Güneykent) by utilizing high-resolution satellite imagery and an optimized deep learning–based semantic segmentation approach. In the proposed framework, an enhanced U-Net architecture incorporating asymmetric and dilated convolutional layers was designed to improve parameter efficiency while preserving extensive contextual information. The proposed model, comprising approximately 1.7 million parameters, achieved 88% accuracy, 0.76 Intersection over Union (IoU), and a 0.86 Dice score, demonstrating competitive performance compared to contemporary segmentation models with substantially higher parameter counts. Pixel-level comparison of pre- and post-earthquake imagery revealed reductions in green space reaching up to 89% in the examined sub-regions, with even higher rates observed in certain localized areas. The findings indicate that intensive post-disaster construction and urban reorganization processes may impose substantial pressure on environmental sustainability. The proposed method provides a computationally efficient and scalable decision-support framework for monitoring post-disaster environmental changes and developing sustainable urban planning strategies.
papers.venue: Journal of the Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Monitoring of Tea Plant Growth and Nitrogen Status Using UAV Multisource Remote Sensing Features
papers.abstract: Accurate and efficient monitoring of tea plant growth parameters via remote sensing is essential for precision plantation management. However, spectral indices relying solely on reflectance often exhibit limited sensitivity in capturing complex tea canopy characteristics. This study developed a data-driven framework integrating spectral reflectance, frequency-domain harmonic components, and spatial texture features to construct tri-feature fusion indices (TFIs) and establish machine learning and deep learning models for tea growth monitoring. Ten-band multispectral imagery was acquired using a UAV alongside synchronous field measurements of leaf and plant biomass and nitrogen accumulation. TFIs were constructed through exhaustive feature combinations and optimized via a data-driven search strategy. Subsequently, random forest (RF), multilayer perceptron (MLP), convolutional neural network (CNN), and transformer models were evaluated using a leave-one-site-out cross-validation (LOSO-CV) strategy. The selected TFIs showed strong associations with tea growth parameters within the investigated dataset, with R2 values up to 0.63 and 0.62 for leaf dry matter and leaf nitrogen accumulation, respectively. Models incorporating selected TFIs achieved cross-validated R2 values of 0.56 for leaf dry matter (MLP), 0.59 for plant dry matter (MLP), 0.73 for leaf nitrogen accumulation (MLP), and 0.68 for plant nitrogen accumulation (CNN). These models exhibited competitive predictive performance comparable to RF, although no statistically significant differences in mean absolute error were observed under site-held-out evaluation. Furthermore, model-derived spatial maps provided insights into fine-scale spatial heterogeneity and potential interannual variations in tea growth parameters across representative plantations from 2024 to 2025. Overall, this study provides a UAV-based framework for tea growth parameter estimation by integrating multi-domain information without requiring additional environmental observations.

papers.title: Detecting soil moisture drought impacts on ecosystem physiology from earth observation data
papers.abstract: Abstract. Satellite remote sensing is widely used to monitor vegetation drought impacts, yet water stress triggers both structural changes and physiological adjustments, whose relative importance varies across space and time. Structural responses, captured by multispectral vegetation indices are well documented, while the extent to which readily available satellite data can detect physiological drought effects remains insufficiently quantified. Here, we assess how much information on drought-induced physiological responses is contained in multispectral reflectance, land surface temperature (LST), and climate reanalysis data. We combine MODIS reflectance and thermal data with an ERA5-Land potential cumulative water deficits metric (PCWD), and train a machine-learning model using eddy covariance data. The target variable represents drought-induced reductions in light use efficiency (fLUE), explicitly separating physiological regulation from structural canopy changes. Our resulting data-driven model captures variations in drought-related physiological response more accurately than previously documented indices commonly applied for drought monitoring (R² = 0.64, RMSE = 0.112, spatial cross-validation). Application across central Europe during two recent summers demonstrates that the model detects drought impacts on photosynthesis earlier and more sensitively than NDVI, particularly in evergreen ecosystems where structural signals are muted. Our results show that a systematically trained, data-driven integration of multispectral reflectance, thermal signals, and climate data can extract a substantial portion of the physiological drought response from Earth observation data. This approach enables a more confident and spatially consistent assessment of drought impacts on photosynthesis using the full combined information content of satellite and climate datasets, beyond what structural vegetation indices alone can provide.
keywords: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

papers.title: Monitoring desertification dynamics and transition patterns through spatial-frequency feature integration of remote sensing data: a case study of the Gurbantunggut Desert, China
papers.abstract: One of the most severe types of land degradation in arid and semi-arid regions is desertification, which poses serious risks to ecological security, sustainable development, and the global climate system. However, long-term remote sensing monitoring is challenged by gradual transitions between different desertification levels and the ambiguity of spatial boundaries, leading to substantial uncertainty in fine-grained identification and quantitative assessment. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Deep Semantic Change Detection Network (DSCD-Net) that integrates spatial and frequency feature representations for fine-grained desertification monitoring using multi-temporal Landsat images acquired from 1990 to 2020. The framework takes bi-temporal multispectral images as inputs and directly predicts pixel-level desertification transition relationships, thereby accurately representing the location, direction, and intensity of changes. The proposed framework was applied to the Gurbantunggut Desert, China, to examine long-term desertification dynamics and transition patterns. Experimental results show that DSCD-Net achieved 92.11% OA, 78.18% mIoU, 74.36% Fscd, and 34.75% SeK, outperforming the comparison methods. Long-term analysis shows that the evolution of desertification in this region exhibits significant nonlinear characteristics and periodic fluctuations, with the moderate desertification state as a key transitional phase. Furthermore, precipitation during the snow accumulation and melting period is identified as the dominant climatic driver regulating desertification dynamics. By explicitly capturing transition pathways and intensity, the proposed framework provides a process-oriented ecological indicator framework for assessing land degradation and offers valuable support for ecological restoration planning and sustainable land management in arid environments.

papers.title: Oil Palm Detection from High Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery with Improved YOLO Deep Learning Frameworks
papers.abstract: Purpose: Most existing oil palm detection studies rely on standard You Only Look Once (YOLO) models without architectural modifications, limiting their detection performance. This study aims to improve the YOLO11 model for oil palm detection by integrating various attention mechanisms.Research Method: A total of 53,113 annotations of WorldView-2 and UAV datasets were used for training (80%), validation (10%), and testing (10%). An external validation dataset was included to evaluate model generalizability to different tree crown sizes and spatial characteristics (young oil palm, mature oil palm, mixed land cover). To improve the YOLO11 model, attention modules such as Coordinate Attention (CA), Efficient Channel Attention (ECA), and Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) were integrated into the neck component. Model evaluation was conducted in terms of accuracy assessment and processing times.Findings and Values: For the primary dataset, YOLO11-CBAM achieved the highest mAP50-95 for validation (0.605) and testing (0.611). For the external validation dataset, YOLO11-CBAM also achieved the highest Recall and F1-score for both the young oil palm region (Recall: 0.988, F1-score: 0.992) and the mixed land cover region (Recall: 0.924, F1-score: 0.953). However, YOLO11-ECA achieved the highest accuracy across all metrics for the mature oil palm region. This study demonstrates that adding attention modules to the YOLO11 architecture improves detection accuracy and generalization despite the slightly increased inference time. The attention-enhanced models outperformed the baseline model and benchmark detectors (Faster R-CNN, RetinaNet) in oil palm detection across different environmental conditions.
papers.venue: Journal of Agricultural Sciences – Sri Lanka
papers.publisher: Sabaragamuwa University, Faculty of Agricultural Sciences

papers.title: Remote Sensing Change Detection using ArcGIS: A Comparative Study Of Methods Applied to Urban Expansion in Baghdad City
papers.abstract: Third world countries often suffer from poor urban planning and unregulated construction including the conversion of agricultural land into residential commercial or industrial areas. Middle Eastern countries in particular are among the leaders in this trend actively transforming farmland into residential zones. This study focus on comprehensive evaluation of three methods of remote sensing techniques change detection within the ArcGIS program environment specifically to study urban expansion in Baghdad province over a 20-year period (2004–2024). The goal of our study identifies the basic preprocessing steps necessary to remove external influences and examines the theoretical foundations of image subtraction image ratio and subsequent classification followed by their practical application using satellite image analysis tools and the spatial analyzer in ArcGIS software. Image subtraction methods are conceptually simple and easy to implement using the ArcGIS raster calculator. They effectively reduce background noise while enhancing contrast features making them suitable for monitoring large-scale changes in peripheral desert areas. However they do not provide classificatory information about the types of changes occurring. Image ratios perform well in monitoring changes in vegetation cover and soil conditions, which is crucial for agricultural areas surrounding Baghdad Governorate although they fall short in accurately identifying land cover shifts. A subsequent comparison of classifications conducted using maximum likelihood classification and merging tools in ArcGIS enables the identification of start-to-end change trajectories. The findings reveal that urban and industrial areas in Baghdad expanded from approximately 8.5% to 11.8% of the study area between 2004 and 2024 while vegetation cover declined from 16.53% to 9.3% over the same period. The ArcGIS application provides researchers with a flexible and reproducible framework for analyzing changes in Iraqi cities, highlighting the strengths and weaknesses of each methodology employed in semi-arid urban environments.
papers.venue: Journal of education for pure science.

papers.title: SRS-DETR: DETR for small object detection in remote sensing images
papers.abstract: Abstract In the field of remote sensing image processing, small object detection presents a significant challenge due to the diminutive size of the objects, limitations in image resolution, and the difficulty of recognizing objects within complex backgrounds. To address these challenges, we propose a novel small object detection model for remote sensing images, named SRS-(DETR) DEtection TRansformer. This model is a variant of the DETR. Firstly, we introduce the Deformable Feature Correlation module to mitigate the high computational cost associated with the Multi-head Self-Attention mechanism in the transformer encoder and to enhance the performance of the model in detecting small objects. Secondly, we propose the Dynamic Multi-scale Sequence Fusion (DMSF) module. This module employs a dynamic design to efficiently fuse features at different scales, further improving the ability of the model to detect small objects. Finally, we design an Intersection over Union (IoU) loss function, Dynamic Multi named GWIoU, specifically tailored for small object detection in remote sensing images, to optimize the training process. Experimental results demonstrate that the mAP of SRS-DETR reaches 85.3%, 97.5%, and 96.3% on the LEVIR-Ship, SSDD, and RSOD datasets, respectively. Our model outperforms current popular detection methods for remote sensing images. Overall, the transformer-based architecture of SRS-DETR exhibits superior detection performance and generalization capability. Overall, the transformer-based architecture of SRS-DETR achieves excellent detection performance and sound generalization capability on the three datasets employed in this study.
keywords: Advanced Image and Video Retrieval Techniques

papers.title: SnowMapPy: An automated GEE Python tool for snow cover mapping and monitoring in the Moroccan Atlas Mountains
papers.abstract: SnowMapPy is an open-source Python-based package developed to streamline the collection, processing, and analysis of MODIS snow cover data from Terra and Aqua satellites. By automating essential steps, including data clipping, reprojection, filtering, and time series generation, SnowMapPy significantly enhances the efficiency and precision of snow hydrology research. The package allows users to collect and process data directly from Google Earth Engine, enabling efficient data acquisition and processing tailored to the needs of snow hydrology, water resource management, and climate change studies. Designed for accessibility and flexibility, SnowMapPy supports large-scale, high-resolution snow cover analysis with minimal configuration. Through its modular structure, the package facilitates customized workflows, making it a valuable tool for researchers aiming to understand snow dynamics and its impact on seasonal water resources. The first application of SnowMapPy was in the Moroccan Atlas Mountains, where snowmelt is essential for water resources. The tool effectively captures spatial and temporal snow cover variations, offering valuable insights for water management and climate impact assessments. This initial implementation highlights its potential for broader application in other snow-covered regions worldwide.

papers.title: Assessing Built-up Land Disparities in the Uttar Pradesh State Capital Region: A Sentinel-2 NDBI-Based Analysis
papers.abstract: The Uttar Pradesh State Capital Region, notified in July 2024, brings six districts around Lucknow under one planning framework, yet its built environment has not been described at the regional scale. This study maps built-up land using Sentinel-2 imagery. Nine near-cloud-free Level-2A scenes acquired in October 2025 were mosaicked, masked by district and processed using the Normalized Difference Built-up Index, with classified extents checked against high-resolution reference imagery. Built-up intensity ranges from 10.11 per cent of district area in Unnao to 26.89 per cent in Lucknow, with a coefficient of variation of 36.8 per cent. The regional Gini coefficient of 0.159 indicates relatively low inequality in the distribution of built-up land. Only Lucknow shows a clearly agglomerated built-up form; elsewhere built-up land remains dispersed. Disparity within the UPSCR is thus expressed more through intensity and spatial form than through distribution, providing a baseline for understanding regional development patterns.
papers.venue: International Journal of Geography Geology and Environment

papers.title: Automated river ice classification of true colour and near-infrared Sentinel-2 satellite data using deep learning
papers.abstract: River ice plays a critical role in the hydrology of cold regions, influencing flood risk, water management, and ecological processes. Ice jam flooding, often triggered during freeze-up and breakup, poses significant hazards to communities and infrastructure. Monitoring river ice is therefore essential for flood forecasting and emergency response. Traditional observation methods, such as field surveys and aerial reconnaissance, face limitations due to safety risks, high costs, and restricted coverage. Optical remote sensing helps overcome these constraints by providing frequent, high-resolution imagery across large and inaccessible rivers. This study develops an automated tool for river ice classification using Sentinel-2 imagery and the YOLOv8 deep learning model. A dataset of 1748 labelled 4 km × 4 km images from the Peace and Athabasca Rivers, representing nine classes: border ice, frazil slush, frazil pans, island/bar, intact ice, open leads, ice jam, ice run, and open water, was used to train, validate and test the model. Two configurations were tested: unimodal using only true colour imagery (TCI) inputs and multimodal using TCI and near-infrared (NIR) band 08 inputs. The multimodal configuration improved detection and segmentation mAP@0.5 to 87% and 83%, respectively, outperforming the unimodal configuration (84% and 80%). Incorporating NIR enhanced the separability of challenging classes, particularly border ice, which is difficult to delineate due to forming adjacent to islands or bars, and open leads, which are spectrally similar to open water. These findings demonstrate that combining multispectral satellite data with advanced segmentation models enables accurate and large-scale classification of river ice. This approach offers a practical tool to support near-real-time river ice monitoring, enhance flood forecasting, and improve decision-making in cold-region river systems.

papers.title: Nuclear Safety Monitoring Under Restricted Access: A Remote Sensing and OSINT Approach to the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant
papers.venue: Remote Sensing Applications Society and Environment

papers.title: Advancing Sustainable Livestock Manure Management: A Systematic Review of DSS, Variables, and Spatial Dimensions
papers.abstract: The intensification of livestock production has amplified the need for sustainable manure management strategies to mitigate environmental impacts and support circular economy principles. This systematic review investigates the global landscape of decision-support systems (DSS) developed for livestock manure management, focusing on their spatial scale of application, input variables, validation approaches, typological architectures, operational maturity, and interoperability capabilities. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a total of 31 peer-reviewed studies published between 2006 and March 2026 were analysed. Results reveal a predominance of contributions from a limited number of countries, particularly in Europe and North America, with DSS implementations spanning both farm-scale—aimed at optimizing operational efficiency—and territorial-scale—supporting regional nutrient-flow coordination and policy-oriented environmental planning. Frequently used variables include manure characteristics, climate and soil data, livestock types, and crop requirements. However, validation procedures and operational readiness levels remain heterogeneous across the analysed studies, and most systems remain fragmented, lacking full integration across the manure management chain. The review proposes a structured typological classification of DSS architectures and a comparative framework linking validation strategies, operational maturity, and interoperability across spatial scales. Key challenges include limited cross-platform interoperability, region-specific calibration, and insufficient real-time responsiveness. Future developments should prioritise adaptable multi-scale DSS integrating artificial intelligence, remote sensing, and geospatial analysis, while participatory approaches will be essential to ensure practical relevance and support sustainable agricultural transitions.

papers.title: Coastal dynamics in a climate change context: Evidence from Demak regency, Indonesia
papers.abstract: Climate change contributes to sea-level rise, tidal flooding, and shoreline erosion in many coastal regions worldwide. Demak Regency, located on the northern coast of Central Java, Indonesia, has experienced significant coastal environmental change over the past three decades. This study examines the spatio-temporal dynamics of the Demak coastline over a 30-year period through analyses of shoreline change, coastal vulnerability levels, and tidal inundation. Four multi-temporal Landsat images acquired in 1993, 2003, 2013, and 2023 were analyzed using the Digital Shoreline Analysis System (DSAS) to quantify shoreline change, the Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) to map inundation extent, and a Coastal Vulnerability Index (CVI) based on three physical parameters. The results indicate severe shoreline erosion, particularly in Sayung Subdistrict, where the mean End Point Rate (EPR) reached −32.92 m/year. Approximately 56% of the Demak coastline falls within the very high vulnerability category, particularly in areas experiencing severe shoreline retreat and extensive inundation. Tidal inundation expanded substantially across the coastline, with Sayung recording the largest cumulative increase in inundated area, reaching approximately 3946 ha. These findings demonstrate extensive coastal degradation and ongoing loss of productive coastal land, with important implications for the economic, social, and ecological resilience of coastal communities.

papers.title: Remote sensing for precision forestry: detection and counting of Eucalyptus saligna trees using multispectral RPAS imaging and the YOLOv8n computer vision algorithm
papers.abstract: Abstract The integration of intelligent systems for processing forest data is advancing, offering a promising approach to enhance the efficiency and sustainability of the forestry sector. However, there is currently a lack of rapid and accurate methods for tree counting during the initial phase of Eucalyptus plantations. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the use of the You Only Look Once version 8 nano (YOLOv8n) algorithm to detect and estimate the count of Eucalyptus trees 180 days post-planting, using high resolution multispectral imagery. The study area consisted of a 7.09 ha commercial Eucalyptus saligna plantation located in southern Brazil. The identification and delimitation of E. saligna tree crowns for training and validation of the model were performed using multispectral images obtained by a Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS). For detection and count estimation, the YOLOv8n algorithm was used. For model evaluation, 70% of the dataset was allocated for training and 30% for validation, achieving a recall of 0.93 and an mAP50 of 0.92. Subsequently, the model was employed to predict and estimate the tree count in an independent test area (4.45 ha). The final validation metrics yielded a recall of 0.915, mAP50 of 0.722, true positive rate of 78.15%, and false positive rate of 13.61%, with a relative error of 4.78%. The YOLOv8n model proved to be promising in the detection and count of E. saligna trees during the initial phase of the plantation, offering potential support for assessing survival rates, as well as for monitoring growth and estimating wood volume.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal analysis of urban expansion and environmental impacts in five Saudi Arabian cities by utilizing geospatial and remote sensing approach
papers.abstract: Rapid urbanization in Saudi Arabia has fundamentally reshaped metropolitan landscapes, creating unprecedented challenges for environmental sustainability in arid regions. This study presents a spatiotemporal analysis of urban expansion patterns and associated environmental impacts across five major Saudi cities (Riyadh, Makkah, Jeddah, Madinah, and Dammam) over a 30-year period (1993-2023) using remote sensing and geographic information systems (GIS). We employed supervised classification of multi-temporal Landsat imagery, integrating spectral indices such as NDVI, SAVI, and NDWI to enhance land-cover discrimination. Classification accuracies ranged from 92% to 95.2% and were validated through stratified sampling and error matrix analysis. Post-classification change detection algorithms quantified urban growth dynamics, while binary logistic regression models assessed topographic influences on spatial development patterns. Results reveal dramatic urban transformation across all study cities. Madinah experienced the largest absolute expansion (759.2 km²), followed by Riyadh (648.08 km²) and Jeddah (640.12 km²). Growth rates varied significantly: Riyadh exhibited the highest proportional increase (236.8%), while Makkah showed more constrained expansion (48.92 km²) due to topographic limitations. Spatial analysis identified distinct urbanization patterns, with centralized growth in Makkah and Madinah versus dispersed, sprawling development in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam. Topographic analysis showed that slope significantly influenced urban development in Jeddah (p = 0.003) and Makkah (p = 0.030), while elevation significantly shaped expansion patterns in Riyadh, Jeddah, Makkah, and Madinah (p < 0.05). Model fit statistics (Nagelkerke R² = 0.06-0.24; ROC AUC = 0.56-0.72) indicate that topographic variables provide modest but meaningful explanatory power, with additional socioeconomic variables needed for comprehensive modeling. These findings reveal complex relationships among urban growth, topographic constraints, and environmental pressures in arid metropolitan areas. The observed urban expansion patterns are consistent with documented effects of government polici…

papers.title: Climatic Constraints and Thermal Adjustment Shape the Apparent Response of Ecosystem Photosynthetic Optimum Temperature to Growth Temperature
papers.abstract: Abstract The apparent optimum air temperature at which ecosystem gross primary productivity (GPP) peaks () exhibits a globally observed positive correlation with local growth temperature, represented by growing‐season‐averaged daily maximum temperature (). Despite recognition of this spatial covariation, the drivers underlying this variability remain unclear. Combining in situ and satellite‐derived GPP measurements, we find that growth temperature is a stronger large‐scale correlate of than plant functional type (PFT) identity, while the magnitude of the ‐to‐ sensitivity varies among PFTs. This strong dependence on growth temperature is reproduced by a simple, mechanistic photosynthesis model and an ensemble of Dynamic Global Vegetation Models. We then conducted factorial simulations to test two overarching mechanisms that may underlie the emergent – relationship: biochemical thermal adjustments (acclimation and adaptation) of photosynthetic capacity and suboptimal meteorological conditions. The results show that the observed relationship cannot be attributed to either mechanism alone. Biochemical thermal adjustment contributes substantially to the drawdown of apparent in boreal and some temperate regions, while suboptimal environmental conditions, including co‐occurring high vapor pressure deficit, limited light, and infrequent occurrence of physiologically favorable temperatures, also constrain the diagnosed optimum, with their relative contributions varying markedly among regions. These findings caution against interpreting the apparent –growth‐temperature relationship as a direct measure of intrinsic physiological acclimation or long‐term ecosystem resilience.
keywords: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

papers.title: An intelligent data-processing and machine learning workflow for urban heat assessment in smart cities
papers.abstract: Smart city management relies on practical and repeatable ways to turn spatial data into information that planners can use. Sofia, Bulgaria, was selected as a test area for the proposed satellite-based urban heat assessment. The work uses 14,400 grid observations prepared in Google Earth Engine for June 1–September 15, 2024. The dataset combines Landsat 8/9 land surface temperature, NDVI, NDBI, MODIS albedo and geographic coordinates. These variables were examined through correlation analysis and used for regression model comparison with train-test validation, five-fold cross-validation and spatial block cross-validation. Gradient Boosting achieved the best result with R² = 0.886, mean cross-validation R² = 0.890 ± 0.004 and spatial block validation R² = 0.830 ± 0.035. An additional 2023 check confirmed the same best-performing model but with lower validation scores, showing that model performance is year-dependent. The workflow supports early-stage identification of priority areas for green infrastructure.
papers.venue: International Journal on Information Technologies and Security

papers.title: Urban Expansion and Thermal Transformation in the Greater Kumasi Sub-Region, Ashanti Region, Ghana
papers.abstract: Rapid urban expansion is reshaping land cover and surface thermal conditions across many sub-Saharan African cities. This study examined land-use and land-cover change and land surface temperature dynamics in the Greater Kumasi Sub-Region, Ghana, between 2004 and 2024. Landsat imagery for 2004, 2014, and 2024 was classified using a Support Vector Machine algorithm. LST was retrieved using a single-channel approach with NDVI-based surface-emissivity correction. Thermal changes, land-surface associations, administrative variations, and population exposure were analyzed utilized spectral indices, Pearson correlation, zonal statistics, and WorldPop data. Built-up land increased from 29,855 ha to 84,152 ha, representing a 181.87% increase, mainly through the conversion of open vegetation and farmland. Mean LST rose from 25.88°C to 29.23°C, with 3.12°C of the 3.35°C increase occurring between 2014 and 2024. Areas with LST ≥27°C expanded from 8.93% of the valid mapped area in 2004 to 92.80% in 2024, although the smaller valid raster extent in 2004 requires cautious interpretation. In 2024, LST was positively associated with built-up and bare surfaces and negatively associated with vegetation and water-related surfaces. Approximately 84.02% of the estimated population was located within high or very high LST zones. Densely developed districts recorded the highest LST, while several peri-urban administrative units experienced the fastest warming. The findings support stronger development control, protection of connected green infrastructure, and targeted heat-mitigation measures in rapidly warming and densely populated districts.

papers.title: Zonal Patterns of Change in Vegetation Cover and Soil Moisture in Typical Tundra under Climate Warming Conditions (A Case Study of the Marresal Area, Yamal Peninsula)
papers.abstract: Under climate warming, the intensity of permafrost transformation process depends on many factors, including topography, landscape types, vegetation cover, and soil composition and moisture. Therefore, the author considers it relevant to identify the factors that most significantly influence permafrost stability, as well as to determine surface properties (indicators) that characterize its degradation. The aim of the study is to assess how climate warming alters vegetation properties and soil moisture across different landscape types and geomorphological levels, and to evaluate the relationship between these changes and geocryological conditions. The analysis is based on Landsat satellite data acquired between 1985 and 2024 for an area of typical tundra on the western coast of the Yamal Peninsula. Vegetation and moisture dynamics were quantified using the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI), and the temperature-vegetation soil moisture index (WI, Wet Index). The identified trends in the indices show a dominant influence of topography on the rate of soil moisture and vegetation cover growth. Thus, the change rates of indices can be considered as indicators of changes in the depth of the seasonal thaw layer.

papers.title: A machine learning model for estimating tree age based on trunk radius and radial growth rate
papers.abstract: Due to substantial differences in radial growth among tree species and environments, accurate tree age estimation remains challenging. This study developed a generalized multi-species tree age estimation framework by incorporating approximate relative radial growth rate ( RGR ) into machine learning and ensemble models. A total of 186 stem discs from four tree species were collected at a sampling height of 1.3 m above ground. Annual rings were sequentially grouped from the outermost ring toward the pith to derive stem radius ( R ), age at the sampling height, average annual-ring width ( AAW ), and RGR . Four machine learning models, including Backpropagation Neural Network, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and Support Vector Regression, were trained using R and RGR as input variables, and their predictions were integrated using a weighted ensemble strategy. The ensemble model achieved an R 2 of 0.865, a prediction accuracy of 85.5%, an RMSE of 4.318 years, and an MAE of 3.058 years. Compared with the model using R and TreeSpecies , incorporating RGR increased R 2 from 0.589 to 0.865 and reduced RMSE from 7.345 to 4.318 years. These results indicate that RGR partially reduces the model’s dependence on explicit species information. The proposed framework shows potential for multi-species tree age estimation and provides a basis for developing generalized large-scale models for tree age estimation.

papers.title: Bespoke Precision Agriculture for Small‐Scale Farming in Sub‐Saharan Africa: Defining Potential Benefits and Pathways
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Precision agriculture (PA) holds enormous potential for smallholder farmers in sub‐Saharan Africa (SSA), where agriculture remains central to economic development, employing more than half of the adult population and contributing significantly to GDP. However, adoption rates remain low. This communication examines the potential benefits, challenges and possible pathways for increasing uptake among smallholders in SSA. Drawing from recent initiatives and case studies, successful applications demonstrate that low‐cost, localised and gender inclusive PA innovations can increase adoption among smallholders. However, challenges such as high upfront technology costs, limited internet connectivity, low digital literacy, limited access to financial services and a lack of tailored training remain significant barriers. Addressing these barriers requires the co‐creation of affordable technologies and flexible financing schemes, the provision of support services, offline functionality and integrating PA into the educational curriculum and extension systems in SSA to build capacity to sustain adoption. Furthermore, promoting gender inclusivity and strengthening data management systems are equally important for long‐term success. By addressing these barriers, PA can drive sustainable agricultural production, improve food security and enhance climate resilience. This communication highlights the need for coordination among farmers, developers, researchers and policymakers to foster a robust PA ecosystem for smallholder farmers in SSA.

papers.title: Digital Frontlines: Innovation for Food and Water Resilience in Humanitarian Contexts
papers.abstract: Humanitarian crises, resulting from conflicts, climate change, displacement, and environmental shocks, continue to put food and water security at risk for millions of vulnerable populations globally. Digital technologies are increasingly being used at the “digital frontlines” of humanitarian work to enhance food and water resilience. This paper explores the contributions of developing digital innovations including mobile and SMS systems, remote sensing, Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, drones, blockchain, AI, digital cash transfers, and data dashboards, to humanitarian food and water activities. An integrative review approach is employed in synthesizing evidence from humanitarian contexts and analyzing eight case studies from across Africa, Asia and global disaster settings. The research reveals significant benefits to early warning, efficiency in service delivery, aid targeting, reduction in costs, transparency, and community engagement. Key results include decreased downtime in water infrastructure, enhanced prediction in food insecurity, effective cash-transfer operations, and better water quality control. Challenges remain to implementation due to infrastructural limitations, digital exclusion, data protection issues, interoperability, low local capacity, and insufficient longer-term funding. Operational and cost-efficiency gains appear to be substantiated but there is still a lack of evidence-based assessments of longer-term resilience outcomes. To achieve effective institutionalization of digital humanitarian innovation, the paper suggests strengthened governance structures, ethical guidelines, participatory design, long-term investment, and enhanced partnerships among governments, humanitarian organizations, private sector actors and local communities. In conclusion, digital innovations can play a significant role in reinforcing humanitarian resilience and achieving the SDGs on food security, water and climate adaptation.
papers.venue: International Journal of Applied Research in Business and Management
keywords: Food Security and Health in Diverse Populations

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Water, Sanitation and Hygiene in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Review of Applications, Opportunities and Challenges
papers.abstract: Water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) remain critical public health and development challenges in SubSaharan Africa (SSA), where approximately 440,000 deaths from diarrheal diseases were recorded in 2024 alone, primarily due to water contamination by fecal pathogens. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as transformative tools with the potential to address long-standing WASH challenges across the region. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the current state of AI applications in WASH across SSA, examining five key domains: water quality monitoring and prediction, sanitation infrastructure assessment, waterborne disease surveillance, citizen science and community engagement, and decision support for water resource management. Drawing upon peer-reviewed literature published between 2020 and 2026, alongside contemporary case studies from across the region, the review identifies significant opportunities including improved predictive accuracy for contamination events, scalable monitoring through remote sensing, and enhanced community participation through AI-powered tools while also highlighting persistent challenges, including data scarcity, infrastructural deficits, limited technical capacity, and ethical concerns around algorithmic governance. The analysis reveals that while AI-driven solutions have demonstrated substantial promise in research settings, translation to widespread operational deployment remains constrained by systemic barriers.
